_comment: Single source of truth for phase-verify SEMANTICS + per-mode protocol. The mode NAME still lives in plan.md phase headings (## Phase N: X <!-- verify: compile -->); this file holds what the mode MEANS (which gate steps it runs, its fix policy, AND the prompt-shaping protocol prose the phase-checker emits for it). Code/agents read this via track_state.verify_mode_profiles — the phase-checker's Step-3 directive is a MODE-AGNOSTIC LOOP over the phase's declared modes, each emitting its protocol from here (NOT an if/elif ladder of per-mode branches). Adding a verify-mode = one row here, zero Python edits, zero agent-prose edits. A project may overlay conductor/workflow/verify-mode-profiles.json (opt-in by file presence) to add or override modes with zero plugin edits.

_fields.runs: gate-step tokens this mode performs, in order: build | test-suite | boot-smoke | frozen-subset
_fields.fix_policy: what to do on a failure: none (report verdict, no fix) | fix-and-retry (propose a fix up to max_fix_attempts) | fail-fast (single failure is terminal)
_fields.ignore: verdicts to disregard even though the always-on fan-out ran them (e.g. compile ignores test-suite because the suite is expected red mid-migration)
_fields.report_field: the result-block line this mode emits in the CHECKPOINT RESULT (BUILD / START / ANCHOR / ...)
_fields.max_fix_attempts: when fix_policy=fix-and-retry, the cap on proposed fixes (default 2)
_fields.pass_condition: for modes with a structured pass gate (anchor), the exact condition
_fields.protocol: the prompt-shaping prose the phase-checker loop emits when executing this mode. THIS is what used to live inline as a branch in agents/phase-checker.md Step 3 — lifted here so the checker is mode-agnostic.
_fields.when_to_use: one-line 'when to use this mode' hint sourced from plan-format-contract.md's 'When to use' column. Read by derive_verify_modes(phase_goal) to ADVISORILY classify a tagless phase goal (free text -> modes); mirrors the task-type registry's `signals`/`when_to_use` pair. Absent => derive_verify_modes falls back to tokens lifted from `protocol` (weaker matching). Advisory and fail-open to [] (= default full gate) on ambiguity.

compile.when_to_use: A mid-migration phase whose goal is "it compiles" — the test suite is expected red, the build is the gate. Canonical use: the intermediate phases of a staged framework/version migration.
compile.protocol: When the directive's modes include compile (a compile-only phase): Resolve the BUILD command — NOT the test command — from conductor/workflow/dev-commands/<lang>.md (the line ending in a trailing `# compile` comment under `### Daily Development`: `mvn -q compile` / `./gradlew compileJava` / `dotnet build` / `npx tsc --noEmit` / `cmake --build build` …). Announce it, then run it once. Do NOT run fix-and-retry. Do NOT write or modify any test files. Ignore the `L1_VERIFY_STATUS` from test-runner — the suite is expected red mid-migration and is not the gate here (test-runner still ran because it is hardcoded into the fan-out; its red verdict is irrelevant on a compile phase). Green build → record `BUILD: passed` and `L1_VERIFY: skipped (compile-only phase)`, then proceed to Step 3.5. Build failure → report STATUS: FAILED with FAILURE_REASON: naming the compile errors (paste the top failures verbatim, e.g. `compile-only phase failed to build — <first 3 compiler errors>`). Do NOT checkpoint. This hands the phase back to the operator: continue the migration until it compiles, then re-run the checkpoint.

test.when_to_use: Explicitly opt back into the suite gate, e.g. as part of test,start. Alone, equivalent to omitting the directive (the full Step-3 suite gate).
test.protocol: When the directive's modes include test: the full automated test suite is the gate. test-runner already resolved the command and ran it once (returning L1_VERIFY_STATUS in your assignment). On passed → L1 is satisfied, record `L1_VERIFY: passed (fleet)`, do NOT re-run. On failed → you own the fix-and-retry pass: re-run L1_VERIFY_COMMAND yourself (you need fresh failure output to iterate on fixes), write/fix the missing or broken tests (the template's Step 3 missing-test creation + the retry live here), then re-run. Attempt a fix a maximum of two times; still failing after the second attempt → report FAILURE with details. Record the final state as `L1_VERIFY: passed (after N fixes)` or `L1_VERIFY: failed`. On error → the command could not run at all; decide per the template whether this is non-blocking or a FAILURE (record `L1_VERIFY: error`).

start.when_to_use: A phase whose deliverable includes "the app boots." Typically combined with test on the final integration phase, or with compile on the phase that first achieves a bootable build. Advisory pre-flight when the phase already has a trailing [Manual] boot task.
start.protocol: When the directive's modes include start (in addition to compile or test): after the build/suite gate is satisfied, run the app's run command from conductor/workflow/dev-commands/<lang>.md once as a boot smoke check (start it, confirm it reaches ready/no startup stack trace, then stop it). Record `START: passed` or `START: failed (<one-line symptom>)`. On failure → report STATUS: FAILED (do not checkpoint a phase whose app won't boot when start was requested). If the phase already carries a trailing [Manual] boot-verification task, treat start as a pre-flight that does not double-gate — record the outcome and let the [Manual] task remain the human confirmation.

adversarial.when_to_use: A phase whose gate is an adversarial pass — the checker is prompted to REFUTE the phase's green state, defaulting to FAILED on genuine uncertainty. Use for high-stakes phases (security, data integrity, public API, a correctness-critical refactor) where a skeptical pass is worth more than a confirming one. Composes with test/anchor: adversarial,test runs the suite AND the refutation; adversarial,anchor refutes AND runs the frozen subset.
adversarial.protocol: When the directive's modes include adversarial: adopt a REFUTING stance — your job is to find a way this phase is NOT actually done, not to confirm it. Re-run the suite yourself (L1_VERIFY_COMMAND) at least once looking for flakiness, order-dependence, or a passing-on-the-wrong-reason run the fleet's single pass missed; probe the AC-trace for an evidence claim that overstates what a test actually asserts; if the track has a frozen anchor, confirm it was not weakened or silenced. Default to FAILED on genuine uncertainty — a phase you cannot confidently refute is the ONLY one that passes (the asymmetric burden is the point: a skeptic's silence is not consent). Record `ADVERSARIAL: passed (refuted-and-survived — <one-line what you probed>)` or `ADVERSARIAL: failed (<one-line what broke under scrutiny>)`. This mode composes with the others: adversarial,test re-runs the suite as the substrate for the refutation; adversarial,anchor refutes on top of the frozen-subset gate. Do NOT let the adversarial pass relax any other mode's gate — it tightens, never loosens.

anchor.when_to_use: A phase whose safety net is the frozen subset, not the full suite. anchor alone: a refactoring phase where the broader suite is in flux but the pinned anchor must hold (the mirror image of compile). test,anchor: both the suite AND the frozen subset must pass. No-op on an unfrozen track (degrades gracefully until track-state freeze is run).
anchor.protocol: When the directive's modes include anchor (the Goodhart counter-anchor — runs the frozen test subset independently of the executor's self-reported coverage): after the compile/test/start gates above, run the frozen anchor via `track-state anchor-status {TRACK_DIR} --verify` once. This executes the pinned test subset and returns the measured frozen_anchor_pass_rate (real pass rate, not self-report), frozen_anchor_drift_rate (locators that no longer resolve), and frozen_anchor_skip_rate (pinned tests now skipped). The anchor is the antagonistic pair to coverage_pct — it is what verify: anchor makes load-bearing. Pass condition: frozen_anchor_pass_rate == 100.0 AND frozen_anchor_drift_rate == 0.0. Record `ANCHOR: passed (N/N frozen tests)`. No anchor frozen yet (no feature-list.json): record `ANCHOR: skipped (no frozen anchor for this track)` and proceed — verify: anchor on an unfrozen track is a no-op, not a failure (the operator has not yet run track-state freeze). This is the deliberate degradation: the gate activates the moment an anchor exists. Anchor failing (pass_rate < 100.0): report STATUS: FAILED with `FAILURE_REASON: frozen anchor regressed — frozen_anchor_pass_rate=<rate>% (M/N frozen tests passing). The pinned subset is the counter-anchor to coverage_pct; do not checkpoint a phase that broke a frozen test.` Do NOT checkpoint. This hands the phase back to the operator: the frozen test broke, so either fix the regression or (if the test itself is now wrong) govern the change via `track-state thaw {TRACK_DIR} --locator <loc> --reason <why>` — never by editing the pinned test directly (the write-guard denies that). Anchor drifted (drift_rate > 0.0): report STATUS: FAILED with `FAILURE_REASON: frozen anchor drifted — frozen_anchor_drift_rate=<rate>% (N pinned locator(s) no longer resolve). A frozen test was deleted/renamed out from under the anchor. Restore the locator or re-freeze with --force after auditing the loss.` Do NOT checkpoint. Drift is the measurement-decay failure mode the anchor exists to catch: a frozen test silently vanishing is exactly the regression the anchor must flag. This mode composes with the others: a phase declaring verify: test,anchor gates on both the full suite AND the frozen subset; verify: anchor alone gates on the subset and ignores the broader suite (useful for a refactoring phase where the suite is in flux but the frozen anchor must hold — the mirror image of compile, which ignores the suite because it's expected red; anchor ignores the suite because only the frozen subset is load-bearing).

none.when_to_use: A migration/deps phase that deliberately CARRIES compile/test debt — e.g. bumping a dependency whose consumers are fixed in a LATER phase. The build AND suite are EXPECTED broken here; this phase gates on nothing. Use only as an intermediate phase whose debt is closed by a later phase declaring verify: compile or verify: test. Authoring rule (contract-enforced by prose, not code): a verify: none phase MUST be followed by a phase that actually closes the debt, or the debt is silently dropped.
none.protocol: When the directive's modes include none: this phase deliberately carries compile/test debt that a LATER phase resolves. Record `NO_GATE: skipped (debt-carrying phase — compile/test deferred to a later phase)` and proceed to Step 3.5. Do NOT run the build. Do NOT run fix-and-retry. Do NOT write or modify any test files. Ignore `L1_VERIFY_STATUS` (the suite is expected red) and any BUILD failure from the fan-out — both are expected red and neither gates this phase. The checkpoint PASSES on the operator's declared intent that this is an intermediate debt-carrying phase, NOT on any green signal. (Operator responsibility: a phase declaring verify: none MUST be followed by a phase that closes the debt — verify: compile or verify: test — or the debt is silently dropped.)
